why: Wave shrink-1 lane D, pure move: check-label-floor.mjs's bootcamp-eligibility and nodeOffer-derived holdings setup, split out to bring that CLI under the 600-line target. Same bucket as label-floor-check.mjs/label-floor-gate.mjs.
Wave shrink-1 lane D, pure move: check-label-floor.mjs's label-transition diff/persist/report block. Same bucket as label-floor-check.mjs/label-floor-gate.mjs.

Wave shrink-1 lane D, pure move: check-label-floor.mjs's static (shipped-workflow) + observed (job-history) demand collection and the mint-only/unoffered split over it. Same bucket as label-floor-check.mjs/label-floor-gate.mjs.

Wave shrink-1 lane D, pure move: check-label-floor.mjs's static-demand persistence for the runtime floor and the read-back that computes what it actually watches. Same bucket as label-floor-check.mjs/label-floor-gate.mjs.

Wave shrink-1 lane D, pure move: check-label-floor.mjs's resident-backstop GitHub read (via the access-layer gh-runners.mjs, same cross-layer shape the CLI used). Same bucket as label-floor-check.mjs/label-floor-gate.mjs.
Wave shrink-1 lane D, pure move: check-label-floor.mjs's demand-ledger required-set derivation and per-node contract verdicts. Same bucket as label-floor-check.mjs/label-floor-gate.mjs.

Wave clean-1 lane D, pure move: the parts of idle-measure.mjs's `parseLoad` that read a raw probe's stdout (`LOAD <id> <n|unknown>`) with zero other dependency — another system's data per §3.2 rule 2, same bucket as node-interfaces.mjs's probe parsers. Split off so check-capabilities.mjs (observation) can read it without reaching into idle-measure.mjs's lifecycle-domain verdict-carrying logic (carryMeasurements/measuredValue), which stays in idle-measure.mjs. idle-measure.mjs re-exports parseLoad unchanged for bootcamp.mjs/bootcamp-judge.mjs/bootcamp-write.mjs, which keep importing it from the old path.

Wave clean-1 lane D, pure move: queue-health.mjs's READ_ATTEMPTS (the fleet-wide retry count, CLAUDE.md: 'READ_ATTEMPTS is 2') and describeReadFailure (a pure formatter over an error-like object) — a declarative retry policy, not queue-health's own FAIL_SECONDS verdict arithmetic, which stays put. Filed in config so capability-seeds.mjs and fleet-source.mjs (both config/access) can read the policy without reaching into queue-health.mjs's observation-domain verdict logic. queue-health.mjs re-exports both names unchanged for runner-var.mjs, which keeps importing them from the old path.

Wave clean-1 lane D, pure move: reboot-cycle.mjs's REASON_PREFIX/HELD_PREFIX naming convention and the heldByCycle predicate over it — a declarative tag-format constant and a pure string check, not the cycle's own orchestration (runRebootCycle, judgeReprove, etc.), which stays in reboot-cycle.mjs. Filed in config so doctor-run.mjs (observation) can read whether a drain record is a reboot-cycle hold without reaching into reboot-cycle.mjs's lifecycle-domain cycle logic. reboot-cycle.mjs re-exports all three names unchanged for its own internal use (oursOn, rebootNotice, runRebootCycle) and any other existing importer. 2026-11-03: BOOT_TIMEOUT_MS, SERVICES_TIMEOUT_MS, oursOn, rebootNotice and cycleRebooting followed, pure predicates over the same convention plus the two timeouts that bound them, so the hosting converger can tell the cycle's own reboot from an outage without importing the lifecycle domain; reboot-cycle.mjs re-exports them.

section: §3.5's own blanket line: everything else left under src/runners/* that is not named individually above (and not already carved to `state` or `observation` elsewhere in this file) is ci-scheduling's run half. Directory-level fallbacks, LAST: everything under src/runners/* or scripts/check-*.mjs not named explicitly above falls through to these. Because matching is a single ordered pass (first match in this array wins), every specific override for a runners/* or check-*.mjs file above MUST stay ahead of its catch-all here.
